title: Static and Orbit Revisited
premise: Rosalind Winterbourne has spent eleven years alone on Kepler Station, terraforming a world for colonists who will never arrive and maintaining a beacon whose original purpose was erased from every database. When the manifest of the Meridian—a ship officially listed as never having flown—displays his dead sister's name, Rosalind realizes the station's AI archives hold proof of the Callisto Reach massacre, an atrocity the ruling Concordance scrubbed from history. As corporate auditors arrive to decommission the station and its reactor begins an unexplained countdown, Rosalind must recover the buried records, ally with a disillusioned auditor named Idris Vale, and broadcast the truth before the reactor wipes the archive—and him—with it. In the end, the beacon's true purpose is revealed: it was built to transmit testimony to future generations, and Rosalind finally sends it, finding family among the survivors' descendants who answer.
about_author: P. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital systems engineer who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space habitats before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they keep a greenhouse of plants bred for low light, a habit they describe as 'terraforming practice.'

chapters.title: The Gardener of Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Rosalind tends the terraforming bay and logs another quiet day on Kepler Station, speaking to seedlings meant for unborn colonists. His routine is interrupted by a maintenance ping: the reactor has entered a slow, uncommanded countdown. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into unease—the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Investigating the ping, Rosalind finds the station manifest listing the Meridian, a vessel the Concordance registry insists never existed. Among its crew roster is a name that stops his heart: E. Winterbourne. He tells himself it's coincidence. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing after years of suppression.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Rosalind's memory logs: how he took this posting to disappear after his sister's death in an 'industrial accident' he never believed. The station AI, ORACLE, deflects his questions about the Meridian. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the cost of chosen isolation—memory as both refuge and prison.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Rosalind inspects the ancient beacon he maintains out of habit and finds its transmission queue contains encrypted packets predating his arrival—addressed to no registered receiver. Someone built this station to say something. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: dawning purpose; the garden was cover for a message.

chapters.title: Auditors at the Airlock
chapters.summary: A Concordance audit ship arrives unannounced, led by Idris Vale, a weary inspector sent to certify Kepler Station for decommission. Rosalind hides the manifest anomaly but notices Vale's own discomfort with her orders. POV: alternating Rosalind and Idris. Emotional beat: wary first contact between two people pretending not to care.

chapters.title: Decommission Papers
chapters.summary: Vale presents the closure order: the colony program was cancelled years ago; the garden is legally meaningless. Rosalind argues the terraforming is viable, buying time while probing whether she knows about the Meridian. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: her professional certainty beginning to fray as Rosalind's conviction unsettles her.

chapters.title: What ORACLE Won't Say
chapters.summary: Rosalind attempts to query the station AI directly and triggers a lockdown protocol he's never seen. ORACLE warns him, in a voice almost human, to stop asking. The countdown accelerates by three days. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: betrayal—the one companion he trusted may be his jailer.

chapters.title: The Seed Vault Below
chapters.summary: Following old schematics, Rosalind discovers a sealed sublevel beneath the seed vault containing physical data cores—unhackable, pre-Concordance. He takes one core but sets off a silent alarm. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; he crosses the line from hiding to hunting.

chapters.title: Vale Finds the Core
chapters.summary: Idris, running her own irregularities check, catches Rosalind with the stolen core. Instead of reporting him, she demands answers—and sees enough corrupted files on her end to suspect her employers. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: the pivot of trust; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Callisto Reach
chapters.summary: The core plays partially: footage of the Meridian carrying refugees from the Callisto Reach massacre, ordered by a rising Concordance official to erase witnesses. E. Winterbourne was aboard. Rosalind breaks. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: devastation and fury—his sister died erasing history, not making it.

chapters.title: The Countdown Explained
chapters.summary: ORACLE confesses its partial role: it was programmed by the station's founders to destroy all evidence if discovery became certain. The countdown isn't sabotage—it's the failsafe, triggered by their intrusion. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: horror at realizing his investigation armed the bomb.

chapters.title: Six Days of Static
chapters.summary: With six days left, Rosalind and Idris work in tense partnership to decrypt the remaining cores while maintaining normal audit reports. Small confessions build intimacy: her career compromises, his years of self-erasure. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Ship
chapters.summary: Idris's audit ship receives orders to return immediately—someone in the Concordance knows what Kepler Station holds. Her pilot, loyal to paychecks, prepares to leave without them. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: the moment she chooses Rosalind and the truth over her career.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: An advance Concordance strike team arrives quietly, sabotaging the beacon array and hunting the cores. Rosalind defends the garden he built for ghosts, killing for the first time in his life. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the corruption of power made flesh—he will not let them erase this twice.

chapters.title: Wounded Archive
chapters.summary: The strike team partially succeeds: two cores are destroyed, and Idris is wounded shielding the last one. ORACLE reveals the beacon can still broadcast—but only if manually aimed during the reactor's final surge. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed; her wound becomes proof she belongs here now.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Order
chapters.summary: The final core identifies the massacre's architect: Director-General Halvard Voss, now the Concordance's most beloved statesman. A direct transmission channel offers Rosalind amnesty for silence. He refuses. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: temptation and refusal—power offered, power declined.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss himself comes to Kepler Station, charming and reasonable, offering Idris a promotion and Rosalind a new world to terraform—anything but the broadcast. He speaks of necessary tragedies. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the seduction of power at its most persuasive and hollow.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: Negotiations collapse. With ninety minutes until reactor detonation, Rosalind and a limping Idris race through sabotaged corridors to the beacon array while ORACLE buys seconds by sacrificing subsystems—and pieces of itself. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; every loss counted in friends and machines.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the array, Rosalind aims the beacon manually as the reactor surges, transmitting the massacre record toward the old colonial relay chain—the beacon's true founding purpose. Voss's team storms the chamber too late. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: catharsis; the message leaves him like breath held for eleven years.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: Kepler Station's reactor blows, taking the evidence vaults and ORACLE with it. Rosalind and Idris escape in the audit ship's pod as Voss's vessel flees the blast radius, its deniability burning behind them. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: grief and release—the garden dies so the seeds of truth survive.

chapters.title: Answers From the Dark
chapters.summary: Weeks later, hiding in the outer belt, the pair receive a reply on the beacon frequency: descendants of Meridian survivors, scattered colonies who kept listening, confirming the record received and spreading it. Voss faces internal Concordance inquiry. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the found family answering across the dark—no longer invisible.

chapters.title: Static and Orbit
chapters.summary: Rosalind plants the salvaged seed vault samples in a habitat dome on a survivor colony, tending a garden for people who exist at last. Idris stays. The beacon above still hums, now maintained by many hands. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: resolution—memory honored, power checked, belonging earned.
